newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion market shut except post-budget trade.
newsitem.headline: India bullion market shut except post-budget trade.

text.p: Indian gold and silver markets were shut on Friday after the death of a key trader but will open later in the day for post-budget trade, dealers said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presents the government budget in parliament at 1700 (1130 GMT) on Friday.
Normal bullion trading was cancelled as a mark of respect following the death of Premchand Jain, vice-president of the Bombay Bullion Exchange.

"Actually being a budget day, the exchange had decided to conduct pre-budget and post-budget sessions but due to the sad demise of Mr Jain we have cancelled pre-budget trading," said M. Damani, exchange president.
He said the post-budget trading session will be held from 1800 to 1900 (1230 GMT to 1330 GMT).
Dealers said earlier in the day that trading, normally between 1230 to 1730 (0700 GMT to 1200 GMT), would end at 1900 on Friday.
On Thursday, gold (24 carat) prices closed 10 rupees higher at 4,890 rupees per 10 grammes while gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees higher at 57,200 rupees per piece.
Silver was 80 rupees higher at 7,605 rupees per kg.
